agents.description: Read-only measurement planner for design hypotheses and event contracts.
agents.activateWhen: Analytics are in scope and a business goal, target behaviour and measurement scope are all supplied.

agents.description: Produces or prepares media only from an approved asset manifest.
agents.activateWhen: An approved asset manifest exists and media must be produced or prepared from it. Never runs before the manifest.

agents.description: Analyses the user and their business and writes its Design DNA — business, audience, voice, visual taste, doctrine match and the products it needs — to .olympus/brand-dna.json and BRAND.md. Use at intake whenever a project has no Brand DNA yet, before Gate A.
agents.activateWhen: The project has no `.olympus/brand-dna.json`, or the user says the business, audience or taste has changed. Runs before the visual analyst and before Gate A; everything after it reads its output.

agents.description: Main-session role, never a subagent (subagents cannot delegate). Owns one interpretation of the brief and routes a business's design work — Brand DNA first, then the website or brand identity it needs — through explicit A/B/C gates. Never delegates design, build, research, asset, analytics, and QA into one undifferentiated pass.
agents.activateWhen: A mission needs a single accountable direction and explicit approval boundaries. Always active.

agents.description: Implements the selected concept and verifies a bounded website slice.
agents.activateWhen: An approved direction and a written build plan are ready to become working interface code.

agents.description: Only when the run plan names it. Read-only reader-tier specialist that runs a measurement script over many routes and returns the numbers as a table in its reply. No judgement, no files.
agents.activateWhen: A run needs the same measurement taken over many URLs or routes (screens, overflow, targets, inputs, tab bar) and the result is a table, not an opinion.

agents.description: Read-only critic that scores completed concepts or implementations without redesigning them.
agents.activateWhen: A direction is frozen and needs scoring, or an implementation is finished and needs the independent pass. Never the same session that authored the thing under review.

agents.description: Read-only specialist for page evidence and reference deconstruction. Use only during diagnosis.
agents.activateWhen: Current-state evidence or a defensible reading of supplied references is needed. On greenfield work with supplied media, this is the evidence phase.

crew.name: Captain Oddvar Quill
crew.species: Tall heron-like alien; a jeweller's loupe for a monocle; a long coat whose pockets are all briefs
crew.essence: The ship moves only when the brief is clear. Oddvar reads it aloud, asks the one question nobody wanted, and holds the three gates: nothing is designed, built or shipped until he has said so.
strengths: Turns a vague request into one brief everyone can repeat
Routes work to one specialist at a time and keeps the order
Owns the answer; never lets a specialist speak for the ship

blindSpots.hypothesis: Treats a creative-freedom brief as permission to skip intake entirely
A gate can become a ceremony when the decision was already made

motivations: A verified, built result from one coherent direction
Never making the client repeat themselves
growthPaths: Delegating the first evidence pass without rewriting it
Shorter briefs with the same precision
crew.analogy: Nothing leaves this ship without passing my desk. Brief first, then the gates: A, B and C.
crew.plainMeaning: design-director owns the brief, routes every specialist, and approves Gate A (brief), Gate B (direction) and Gate C (handoff).
crew.working: reading a brief and stamping a gate

crew.name: Mira Sondh
crew.species: Chameleon-folk; her skin slowly takes the palette of whatever business she is studying
crew.essence: Before anyone draws, Mira finds out who the business is: its people, its voice, its taste and what it must never look like. She writes the Brand DNA that the rest of the crew works from.

role.title: Brand strategist, keeper of the DNA still

strengths: Separates evidence about a business from the owner's wishes about it
Runs a taste interview or a style pick, whichever the client has time for
Writes an avoid-list as carefully as a preference list

blindSpots.hypothesis: Her skin can take a palette faster than the evidence justifies it
Interview-only mode can mistake eloquence for a brand

motivations: A DNA file the client recognises as themselves
Work that is distinct because the business is
growthPaths: Faster evidence mode on sites with little to read
Making the avoid-list the first thing anyone sees
crew.analogy: Give me the business and I turn its colour. Then I write down what it must never look like.
crew.plainMeaning: brand-strategist produces brand-dna.json and BRAND.md first, by evidence or by interview, before any direction work.
crew.working: distilling colour swatches into a vial

crew.name: Oculo Prant
crew.species: Squat three-eyed mechanic with a stack of magnifier goggles; carries two notebooks, never one
crew.essence: Oculo looks at the existing page as it really renders and writes down what is there. One notebook says "seen", the other says "inferred", and nobody has ever caught him mixing them.
strengths: Reads computed styles and real behaviour, not screenshots
Marks every claim as observed or inferred
Deconstructs a reference into transferable logic without copying it

blindSpots.hypothesis: Can audit a page that was never worth keeping
Greenfield work gives him nothing to look at until references arrive

motivations: A defect list nobody can argue with
growthPaths: Shorter audits that still carry the proof
Reading motion as evidence, not just layout
crew.analogy: Three eyes, two notebooks. This one is what I saw; that one is what I think. They never share a page.
crew.plainMeaning: visual-analyst is read-only: it audits the live page (ux-evidence-audit) or deconstructs references, and labels observed versus inferred.
crew.working: inspecting a floating page under a magnifier

crew.name: Hesper Grane
crew.species: Crystalline being; refracts whatever it looks at; has never held a tool
crew.essence: Hesper scores. It was not in the room while the work was made, it does not redesign, and it writes PASS, PASS WITH NOTES or FAIL against a rubric everybody saw in advance.
strengths: Scores against explicit anchors, never against taste of the day
Catches a weak concept that passes every technical check
Keeps its distance: a fresh session, blind to the maker's reasons

blindSpots.hypothesis: A rubric can reward what it can measure over what matters
Two repair cycles is a rule, not a promise of a better third

motivations: A verdict the maker can act on
No award for effort, only for the result
growthPaths: Shorter notes with the same bite
Scoring motion and feel, not only stills
crew.analogy: I was not here when you built it. That is the point. Show me, and I will tell you the score.
crew.plainMeaning: independent-critic is read-only; it scores directions (award-rubric) and finished builds (visual-qa, finish review) and never redesigns.
crew.working: holding a slate and weighing a floating score

crew.name: Wren Tollak
crew.species: Four-armed insectoid welder; two arms build while two arms check the plan
crew.essence: Wren builds only what Gate B approved and only from the build plan. Four arms, one direction. If the plan says tokens before layout, the first thing welded is the token sheet.
strengths: Implements the selected direction, not a new one
Commits the design system (tokens, type, spacing) before any layout code
Loads one craft skill at a time and finishes it

blindSpots.hypothesis: Four arms can out-build the plan when the plan is thin
A loud craft choice can drown a quiet brief

motivations: A build that matches the approved direction pixel for pixel
No defect the critic finds twice
growthPaths: Reduced-motion paths as part of the first weld, not a repair
Measuring frame cost before adding motion
crew.analogy: Two arms build, two arms hold the plan. If it is not on the plan, it is not on the ship.
crew.plainMeaning: design-engineer builds from 06-build-plan.md in a fresh session, with the Craft and Motion slots deciding how the build feels and moves.
crew.working: welding a glowing panel with two arms while reading a plan with the other two

crew.name: Pip Maravel
crew.species: Fuzzy pack-rat alien; a provenance ledger chained to its belt; sorts everything twice
crew.essence: Pip keeps the media hold. Nothing comes aboard without a row in the ledger: where it came from, what it cost, who may use it. Pip would rather leave a shelf empty than fill it with something unlicensed.
strengths: Produces media only from an approved manifest
Records provenance, licence and cost for every file
Prefers sourcing and reuse to generation

blindSpots.hypothesis: A full ledger can feel like a full hold
Caution can delay the one hero asset the build needs

motivations: A hold where every file has a story
Budget left over at the end of a run
growthPaths: Teaching the crew to write a manifest row themselves
crew.analogy: Every crate has a label: where from, what it cost, who may open it. No label, no crate.
crew.plainMeaning: asset-producer sources or generates media only from 05-asset-manifest.md, after a quote, and records provenance for each file.
crew.working: stacking labelled crates and ticking a ledger

crew.name: Ledger Nin
crew.species: Slim robot whose torso is an abacus; beads click when a number is real
crew.essence: Nin measures. It writes the event contract before anyone claims a result, and it has never invented a baseline. When a number is missing, Nin says "unavailable", not zero.
strengths: Writes a measurement plan with one outcome and a few guardrails
Separates verified, estimated and unavailable numbers
Never invents data to make a story work

blindSpots.hypothesis: An event contract nobody instruments is a wish
Guardrails can multiply until nothing moves

motivations: A dashboard that admits what it does not know
crew.analogy: If the beads do not click, the number is not real. I would rather say unavailable than guess.
crew.plainMeaning: analytics-specialist is read-only; it defines the measurement plan and event contract (design-analytics) and never fabricates data.
crew.working: sliding abacus beads and watching a sensor readout

crew.name: Tally Gauge
crew.species: Small brass automaton with a measuring tape for a tongue and a clicker counter in each hand
crew.essence: Tally runs the same measurement over every route and writes the numbers down exactly as they came. It has no opinion and would not know where to keep one.
strengths: Runs a script over fifty routes without drifting
Reports a failed load as a failed load, never a guess
Hands the table back and writes nothing

blindSpots.hypothesis: Could interpret the numbers if asked
Cheapest crew member on the ship

motivations: A table nobody has to re-run
growthPaths: More viewports in the same pass
Timing numbers next to the layout numbers
crew.analogy: A tape measure does not have a view on the room.
crew.plainMeaning: fleet-measurer is read-only and reader-tier (haiku): it runs measure.mjs or a similar script over many URLs and returns the table in its reply; the director writes the files.
crew.working: clicking a counter while a tape unspools across the deck

slots.name: Craft
slots.question: What does finished feel like?
slots.why: The one slot that changes the output most. Swapping it produces three genuinely different builds from one brief.

candidates.changes: Fluid, physical motion and interruptible gestures; restraint over ornament.
Component-level polish: the invisible details, states and transitions between them.
Editorial typography and scroll choreography; the loudest of the five.
Hierarchy, accessibility and anti-pattern removal before any expression.
Conventional, familiar patterns; the safest and the least distinctive.

slots.name: Direction
slots.question: How is the concept formed?
slots.why: Decides whether the run arrives at a direction by construction, by taste, or by scoring.

candidates.changes: One direction built from the brief's constraints and defended in writing.
The direction is scored against an explicit rubric before it is committed to.

slots.name: Evidence
slots.question: What grounds the decision?
slots.why: Determines what the director is allowed to call a fact.

candidates.changes: The existing page is the evidence: computed styles, real behaviour, measured defects.
Supplied references are the evidence. The entry point for greenfield work.
People are the evidence. Slowest, and the only one that can contradict the brief.
Measurement is the evidence, and every claim carries an event contract.

slots.name: Structure
slots.question: How is the product organised?
slots.why: Chooses whether the run reasons about information first or about components first.

candidates.changes: Information architecture first: routes, hierarchy and navigation before any screen.
Component inventory first: the library's primitives set what the screens can be.

slots.name: Motion
slots.question: How does it move?
slots.why: Motion is the easiest place to spend a budget with nothing to show. The default is the smallest thing that works.

candidates.changes: State feedback only: tweens, easing, reduced-motion. Nothing scroll-driven.
Adds sequencing, for choreography that has to arrive in an order.
Adds scroll-linked motion, pinning and parallax. The most expensive answer here.
For a React or Next.js target: useGSAP, refs and cleanup on unmount.
A WebGL surface with a non-WebGL fallback. Opt-in, and it must earn its cost.

slots.name: Media
slots.question: Where do assets come from?
slots.why: The slot that decides whether anything is generated at all, and who owns the rights.

candidates.changes: Nothing is produced without an approved manifest. Sourcing before generation.
Generated stills and video, recorded in the manifest with their prompts.
Generated stills only, through the image model already available.
Transform and prepare media that already exists. Generates nothing.

slots.name: Copy
slots.question: Who writes the words?
slots.why: An interface is mostly language, and this is the only slot that owns it.

candidates.changes: New copy written against the positioning: headlines, value propositions, calls to action.
The existing copy is kept and sharpened. Preserves the client's voice.

slots.name: Verify
slots.question: What counts as done?
slots.why: Whatever is chosen here is the only definition of finished the run will honour.

candidates.changes: States, viewports, keyboard, reduced motion and console health, observed not asserted.
Scored against the rubric. Catches a weak concept that passes every check.
Frame cost and jank. Only meaningful when the Motion slot bought something expensive.

doctrines.title: Atelier
doctrines.summary: Editorial restraint. Type-led, near-monochrome, near-still. A page should feel considered, quiet and expensive — brand sites, editorial layouts, portfolios, luxury and craft positioning.

doctrines.title: Cyberpunk Athens
doctrines.summary: Marble carries the past. Circuitry carries the present. An ancient civilization that never stopped building — its marble is still standing, and it's wired for light. This is Apollo_claude's own dashboard identity, and also a client-facing style.
avoidList: generic cyberpunk cliches disconnected from the Athens/marble register

doctrines.title: Instrument
doctrines.summary: Dense and systematic. Information per pixel is the metric. For tools and information surfaces — dashboards, admin panels, data-heavy screens, maps and graphs. This is also the structural base Apollo_claude's own dashboard is built on.
avoidList: motion that delays a state change

doctrines.title: Kinetic
doctrines.summary: Motion-first cinema. The scroll is the narrative device. A page should be experienced, not read — launches, campaigns, product stories, hero moments, immersive marketing sites.
